items.claim: A targeted sampled track nested in two places undoes its own hold
An event track added by `edit` or moved to a new `at` books every past event at once
The booker's cursors pile up for every track and nested offset ever seen, pruned only by a seek
items.note: (moving a nested track back to an old offset also rebooked from that offset's stale cursor; fixed in the same commit)

items.claim: An `edit` to a held track's `weight`, `axes`, or `target` is ignored while the playhead is within its keys
A seek from a handler on a lap's tail fires the landing's events in the same frame
A revived timeline re-registers the first row's mutated seed, `ended: true` included
`rearm` judges direction by the timeline's own scale and ignores the animator's direction
An `edit` that cuts `duration` below the playhead leaves the playhead past the end
Booking with an infinite duration booked every event at clock time NaN and never retimed
A track or nested timeline used in two places was booked at only one of them
A cancel from an event handler during the wrap's tail flush reopened target holds
A cancel from a sampled track's `onTick` reopened later tracks' holds and fired one more event
items.note: This is the same root cause as the line above, so one fix covers both: the sampler stops at a cancel, and the tick returns once canceled.

items.claim: A nested timeline's negative duration counted as 0 for firing but stayed negative for sampling and booking
items.note: All three now read it through a new `length.ts` `nestedLength`.

items.claim: `toClip` wrote a non-finite duration, `at`, `t`, weight or bezier point, which `bindClip` then refused
items.note: I made the strict call (an infinite `duration` throws, naming where) and recorded it in `docs/unruled.md`.

items.claim: `rearm` knew only the forward end, so a timeline finished forward could not be revived to play backward, and one finished backward was revived at 0 and called `onDone` again
A reversed loop that landed exactly on 0 with laps behind it ended, instead of playing on into the lap before
`bindClip` accepted a key with no value, which then threw only when first sampled
